 The optics were bad. Earlier this year videos emerged of men using Ray-Ban Metas (which have camera, audio and AI features) to secretly record and harass women. The backlash against “pervert glasses” was swift. Yet Meta is doubling down on its eyewear—and cameras will remain integral to many AI devices.

Hi Oleg,

The companies building AI infrastructure have hit a wall, and it’s not because of chips.

Power, cooling, and real estate are the real bottlenecks now.

The Compute & Infrastructure Fund offers exposure to companies attacking those constraints from different angles.

The Fund is headlined by Fluidstack, an AI cloud-computing and infrastructure startup that recently signed a $50 billion data center partnership with Anthropic.¹

In September 2026, Fluidstack announced a $1.5 billion round at an estimated $18 billion valuation, more than double its July mark.²

Here’s what else is inside:

- Panthalassa: Floating data centers that are powered and cooled by ocean waves. Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund led a $140M Series B in May 2026 at an estimated $1B valuation.³
- Starcloud: Orbital data centers running NVIDIA GPUs, cooled by space itself. Raised $250M at an estimated $2.3B valuation in August 2026, with NVIDIA and Cisco joining as new investors.⁴
- PsiQuantum: A million-qubit photonic quantum computer, backed by BlackRock, NVIDIA, and Microsoft’s venture fund.⁵
- Stoke Space: A 100% reusable rocket. The U.S. Space Force selected Stoke to compete for national security launches under a $5.6B contract.⁶

There’s no guarantee that revenue, funding, or valuation will continue to grow for these companies, or that they will be profitable. See risk disclosures on the offering page.

With one check, you can gain exposure to key players building the physical foundation for AI’s future.

79667.subject: Higher for longer
79667.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

The 10-year Treasury yield broke out to 5.12% on Wednesday, a level not seen since 2007. This was the largest single-day increase in yields in over a year and the 2nd biggest single-day increase in the MOVE index this year, the measure of bond market volatility. With the Fed having hiked rates last week, and now the whole yield curve shifting up, the bond market reflects expectations and concerns of some combination of inflation, growth, and a growing inability for the Treasury to manage the deficit. Bond markets are pricing yields higher for longer, a notable shift from a year ago, when rate cuts were priced as the base case. How does this move in offchain yields relate to onchain yields, and can the market take it? 

Looking at the spread between onchain stablecoin supply rates and T-bill yields, 2026 is on track to be the most consistently negative year on record. 96.9% of days are negative, with T-bills paying more than onchain lending, exceeding 2023's 89.0%. Stablecoin lending has underpaid bills every day since late April, putting the current period of a discount at the third-longest stretch in history, and the current gap of negative 115 basis points is now in the bottom quintile of its entire history.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5d975eb2-7752-487f-a91a-c73794e03203/image.png?t=1790255332)
Caption: 

When this spread sat in the bottom quintile as it does now, the average 90-day forward change was an +0.85 bps increase. The modal outcome from this current rate context is a nearly 100 bps increase over the coming 90 days. The recent rate hike and shift up in the yield curve have only grown this spread. 

Second, we can look at a recent snapshot of the funding rate term structure on Pendle’s Boros, revealing the market’s implied path of funding rates on BTC and ETH perpetual futures through year-end. Just like the Treasury yield curve, the market prices shorter-term rates at a discount to the long end, showing rates rising out in time.
